question.:question/problem: Which of the following diagrams gives the slope field at the points indicated for the differential equation $\frac{dy}{dx} = 2 - xy$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
We have to sketch the slope field at the points $(-1,2)$,$(1,3)$,$(0,-2)$.

To sketch the slope field at the given points, we substitute their coordinates into the right-hand side of the differential equation.

$$
\begin{aligned} & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(-1,2)}=2-1(-1)(2)=4, \\  & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(1,3)}=2-1(1)(3)=-1, \\  & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(0,-2)}=2-1(0)(-2)=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting up our points and drawing our line segments, we get the following diagram.

$$
\begin{aligned} & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(4,4)}=-2-(-1)(4)(4)=14, \\  & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(2,-2)}=-2-(-1)(2)(-2)=-6, \\  & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(-1,-1)}=-2-(-1)(-1)(-1)=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Which of the following diagrams gives the slope field at the points indicated for the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{(-2)x+(-2)y}{4}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We have to sketch the slope field at the points $(-2,3)$,$(-1,-1)$,$(-3,-1)$.

To sketch the slope field at the given points, we substitute their coordinates into the right-hand side of the differential equation.

$$
\begin{aligned} & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(-2,3)}=\frac{(-2)(-2)+(-2)(3)}{4}=- \frac{1}{2}, \\  & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(-1,-1)}=\frac{(-2)(-1)+(-2)(-1)}{4}=1, \\  & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(-3,-1)}=\frac{(-2)(-3)+(-2)(-1)}{4}=2.\end{aligned}
$$
